teaser: He wanted to renounce the world entirely. The Prophet ﷺ held his doorposts and told him no.
quran_mention: «يَا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّمَا الْخَمْرُ وَالْمَيْسِرُ وَالْأَنصَابُ وَالْأَزْلَامُ رِجْسٌ مِّنْ عَمَلِ الشَّيْطَانِ فَاجْتَنِبُوهُ» — 'wine, gambling, idols and divining arrows are filth, the work of Shaytan, so avoid them' (al-Ma'idah 5:90). Uthman had already refused wine years before the verse came down. When a man recited it to him he said: evil it is, and my insight into it was firm.

layers.title: Who He Was
layers.subtitle: He refused wine before there was a ruling
layers.content:
Uthman ibn Maz'un ibn Habib ibn Wahb ibn Hudhafa, of Banu Jumah of Quraysh. His kunya was Abu as-Sa'ib and his mother was Sukhayla bint al-Anbas. He had two sons, Abd ar-Rahman and as-Sa'ib, by Khawla bint Hakim.

In the Jahiliyya, when drinking was ordinary and expected, he made wine unlawful for himself. His reasoning was not lofty. He said he would not drink anything that takes away his reason, lets men beneath him laugh at him, and gets him to marry his daughter to someone he does not want. Three plain consequences, observed in other men, and enough for him.

Years later the verse in Surat al-Ma'idah came down forbidding it. A man passed him and told him, and recited it. Uthman's answer was almost dismissive of the news: evil it is — my insight into it was firm.

He belonged to a family that would eventually empty out of Makkah. Al-Waqidi records that every one of the family of Maz'un left in the hijrah, the men and the women, none remaining, so that their doors were left locked.
layers.source: Reported from Abd ar-Rahman ibn Sabit and al-Waqidi — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III

layers.title: The Conversion
layers.subtitle: Five men who accepted Islam in one sitting
layers.content:
Yazid ibn Ruman names the group: Uthman ibn Maz'un, Ubayda ibn al-Harith, Abd ar-Rahman ibn Awf, Abu Salamah ibn Abd al-Asad and Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah. They went to the Prophet ﷺ together, he set out Islam and its rulings to them, and all of them accepted at the same time — before he had entered the house of al-Arqam, and before he was calling people there.

That is a very early date. Uthman then made both crossings to Abyssinia, according to Ibn Ishaq and al-Waqidi.

When the Muhajirun reached Madinah the Ansar competed to host them and had to draw lots. Umm al-Ala', one of the women who gave the pledge to the Prophet ﷺ, said simply that Uthman ibn Maz'un came to them in the lots. He was in their house. The Prophet ﷺ marked out the plot for the house of Uthman and his brothers, and Ibn Sa'd notes it was still standing in Madinah in his own day. He was joined in brotherhood to Abu al-Haytham ibn at-Tihan of the Ansar, and he fought at Badr.
layers.source: Reported from Yazid ibn Ruman and Umm al-Ala' — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III

layers.title: With the Prophet ﷺ
layers.subtitle: A door held shut, a wife perfumed
layers.content:
He set a room of his house aside and worshipped in it. The Prophet ﷺ heard, came to the house, took hold of the doorposts and said it two or three times over: Uthman, Allah did not send me with monkhood. The best of people are those on the simple, upright way.

His wife went to visit the Prophet's ﷺ wives and they were troubled by how she looked. They asked what was wrong with her — there was no wealthier man in Quraysh than her husband. She answered: we have none of it. The night, he spends standing in prayer. The day, he fasts. When they told the Prophet ﷺ, he went to Uthman: do you not have a pattern in me? You fast all day and pray all night. Do not do that. Your eye has a right over you. Your body has a right. Your family has a right. So fast, and break your fast.

The next time she came to them she was wearing perfume like a bride. They asked her what had happened. She said: we have what other people have.
layers.hadith_ref: 'Allah did not send me with monkhood' — reported from Abu Qilaba; the correction about the rights of the eye, body and family — reported from Abu Burda, Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Trial
layers.subtitle: His zeal ran ahead of the road
layers.content:
He asked for permission to castrate himself and wander the earth. He said the restraint required of him on campaign was more than he could carry, and he wanted the problem removed.

The Prophet ﷺ refused. Do you not have a pattern in me? I go to my wives, I eat meat, I fast and I break my fast. The castration of my community is fasting — no one in my community castrates or is castrated. In another wording the answer was shorter: no, but you must fast, Ibn Maz'un.

Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said afterwards that if the Prophet ﷺ had allowed him celibacy, he would have gone through with it.

This is a man whose problem was never weakness. He also asked whether he might avoid his wife seeing him unclothed, out of shame. The Prophet ﷺ told him that Allah had made each of them a garment for the other, and that he himself was seen by his own household. Then he turned away and said of him: Ibn Maz'un is modest and chaste. The correction and the praise arrived together.
layers.hadith_ref: 'The castration of my community is fasting' — reported from Ibn Shihab and from Aisha bint Qudama ibn Maz'un; 'Ibn Maz'un is modest and chaste' — reported from Sa'd ibn Mas'ud and Umara ibn Ghurab, Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

layers.title: The Legacy
layers.subtitle: The first grave in al-Baqi', and a stone
layers.content:
He died in Sha'ban, about two and a half years after the hijrah, in the house of Umm al-Ala' who had nursed him. He was the first Muslim buried at al-Baqi'. The Prophet ﷺ had chosen the ground himself, walked to the edge of Madinah and said he had been commanded to this place. He set a stone at Uthman's head and called him our forerunner. After that, when anyone died, the question where to bury him got the same answer: with our forerunner, Uthman ibn Maz'un. When one of the Prophet's ﷺ own daughters died — reports differ over which — he said: join our good forerunner. As the bier passed he said, you have gone out and have not worn any of it, meaning this world.

Aisha reported that he kissed Uthman's face after death, and the tears of the Prophet ﷺ fell on his cheek.

And yet when Umm al-Ala' declared that Allah had certainly honoured him, he asked her how she knew. Certainty has come to him, he said, and by Allah I hope for the best for him — but I am the Messenger of Allah and I do not know what will be done with me.
layers.hadith_ref: 'This is our forerunner' and the burial of Uthman ibn Maz'un at al-Baqi' — reported from Ubaydullah ibn Abi Rafi'; the exchange with Umm al-Ala' — reported from Kharija ibn Zayd, Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
layers.source: Ibn Sa'd, Kitab at-Tabaqat al-Kabir, Vol. III, trans. Aisha Bewley

quiz.prompt: What had Uthman ibn Maz'un already decided about wine before any verse forbade it?

options.text: That it was permitted in small amounts
That he would not drink anything that took away his reason
That he would only drink at festivals
That he would sell it but not drink it

quiz.citation: Reported from Abd ar-Rahman ibn Sabit — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: His reasons were practical: it removes your reason, it lets lesser men laugh at you, and it makes you marry your daughter to a man you would not choose. When the verse came, he said his insight into it had been firm.

quiz.prompt: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when he found that Uthman had set a room aside to worship in?

options.text: That he should invite others to join him
That Allah did not send him with monkhood
That the mosque was better
Nothing — he prayed with him

quiz.citation: Reported from Abu Qilaba — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He held the doorposts and repeated it two or three times, then said the best of people are those on the simple, upright way. He did not argue the point; he closed it.

quiz.prompt: How did the Prophet's ﷺ wives find out that Uthman was fasting every day and praying every night?

options.text: He told them himself
His brother reported it
His wife visited them looking neglected and they asked her why
The Prophet ﷺ mentioned it to them

quiz.citation: Reported from Abu Burda — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: They pointed out that no man in Quraysh was wealthier than her husband. Her reply was that they had none of it. After the Prophet ﷺ spoke to him, she came back wearing perfume.

quiz.prompt: What did Uthman ask permission to do, and what was he told instead?

options.text: To live in the mosque; he was told to go home
To castrate himself; he was told that his community's castration is fasting
To divorce his wife; he was told to keep her
To give away all his wealth; he was told to keep a third

quiz.citation: Reported from Ibn Shihab and from Aisha bint Qudama ibn Maz'un — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet ﷺ answered by describing his own life: I go to my wives, I eat meat, I fast and I break my fast. Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas said Uthman would have done it had he been permitted.

quiz.prompt: What was Uthman ibn Maz'un the first Muslim to do?

options.text: To pray in the mosque of Madinah
To be buried in al-Baqi'
To return from Abyssinia
To be given a house in Madinah

quiz.citation: Reported from Ubaydullah ibn Abi Rafi' and from Abdullah ibn Amir ibn Rabi'a — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: The Prophet ﷺ set a stone at his head and called him our forerunner. From then on, when someone asked where to bury the dead, the answer was: with Uthman ibn Maz'un.

quiz.prompt: He gave up wine years before he was told to, on plain reasoning about what it would do to him. What have you cut out on your own judgement?

options.text: Something I saw ruin other people
Something that was costing me time
I only stop when I am told to
I keep meaning to and have not

quiz.citation: Reflection on the report of Abd ar-Rahman ibn Sabit — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: Notice that he did not appeal to piety. He described three concrete outcomes he had seen in other men and refused to be the fourth.

quiz.prompt: His worship was so heavy that his household went without. Which of your commitments is being paid for by someone else?

options.text: My family carries more than they should
My health pays for it
Nothing — I keep it balanced
I had not looked at it that way

quiz.citation: Reflection on the report of Abu Burda — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: The correction was itemised: your eye has a right, your body has a right, your family has a right. None of those rights was described as a concession.

quiz.prompt: He wanted a limit imposed on him rather than have to keep choosing. Where do you wish the decision could be taken out of your hands?

options.text: With food, money or my phone
With relationships
With work I cannot say no to
I would rather keep the choice, even when I fail

quiz.citation: Reflection on Uthman's request and the Prophet's ﷺ refusal — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He was not given the escape, and he was not shamed for wanting it. He was handed a smaller, repeatable discipline instead: fast.

quiz.prompt: 'You have gone out and have not worn any of it,' the Prophet ﷺ said as his bier passed. What of this world would be hard for you to leave unworn?

options.text: Comfort and security
Being respected
Plans I have not finished
People I do not want to leave

quiz.citation: Reported from Abu an-Nadr — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: The words were said about a man from one of the wealthier families of Quraysh, who had left it all in Makkah with the doors locked behind him.

quiz.prompt: When his host declared him honoured by Allah, the Prophet ﷺ asked her how she knew. How do you speak about the dead you loved?

options.text: I say I hope, and leave it there
I say what comforts the living
I find the reserve difficult
I avoid the subject

quiz.citation: Reported from Kharija ibn Zayd from Umm al-Ala' — Ibn Sa'd, Tabaqat Vol. III
quiz.scholar_reflection: He said he hoped for the best for him, then said of himself that he did not know what would be done with him. Ibn Sa'd records that the Companions found this hard to hear about a man like Uthman.
